providers.market_view: The German equity market is navigating a volatile environment characterized by a significant divergence between sectors following the U.S. midterm elections and a dense corporate earnings week. While the primary indices have faced downward pressure due to a sharp reversal in technology and defense stocks—the latter specifically impacted by guidance cuts from key players like Rheinmetall—certain industrial and healthcare names are showing resilience. Sentiment is cautious as investors weigh a cooling macro outlook and geopolitical tensions against robust third-quarter results and raised full-year profitability forecasts in select blue-chip companies. High-volume technical reversals and earnings-driven breakouts are providing isolated long opportunities despite broader index-level headwinds.

# Germany's Continental to become pure-play tire company
...
Continental has announced to sell its ContiTech group sector to an affiliate of Lone Star Funds for 4 billion euros ($4.58 billion), which will turn the German auto parts giant into a pure-play tire manufacturer for the first time in its 155-year history.

The transaction, which is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to finish this year, also includes performance-based components of up to 250 million euros in subsequent years.

The sale of ContiTech, announced on Saturday, is the final step in Continental's realignment.

Nikolai Setzer will step down from the Executive Board by mutual agreement on December 31, 2025, after more than 16 years as a board member and five years as CEO. providers.market_view: The DAX index is showing technical weakness after reaching new all-time highs, with overbought stochastic indicators and a reversal from the 26600 resistance level. The market is experiencing sector rotation away from highly valued technology stocks toward cyclicals and value names following US midterm election results. However, the broader index appears poised for a mean-reversion pullback toward the 26000 support area in the near term, creating a challenging backdrop for new long positions.

German equities head into Friday's Xetra open with a mixed and selective backdrop. Midweek earnings and outlook updates are largely digested, with pharma-led guidance lifts already reflected and defence names volatile on contrasting order strength versus forecast revisions. Pre-market tone looks cautious, with rotation rather than broad momentum and focus shifting to remaining quarterly reports.
